meta.title: Which advertising campaign caused each user’s purchase?
meta.question: Which advertising campaign caused each user’s purchase?
meta.periods: All observed successful charges, April–September 2026 UTC
meta.author: Codex

items: Check numbers refer to the individual JSONL evidence files.
A recorded acquisition source is a first-touch channel, not a campaign or proof of causation.
Purchase
A valid, successful positive non-refund charge; includes subscription renewals and PPV. A later refund does not undo the charge count.
Snapshot
The declared user snapshot instant; it is not a verified database hash.

blocks.text: The campaign that caused each purchase cannot be identified from this database. No campaign-to-user exposure or click link is recorded, and observational attribution alone would not prove causation (checks 4, 6, 10).

items: The data contains 6,215 valid successful charges by 1,465 users, including renewals; no campaign assignment is supported for any of these purchases (checks 7–8, 11).

The recorded first-touch sources are organic 3,023 charges, paid search 1,649, paid social 1,484 and unknown 59. These are descriptive user-level source labels, not purchase-level campaign attribution (check 7).
Independent investigation; no question-specific guides or answer keys were read. The supplied SQLite database was queried read-only.
All available successful charges, effective 2026-04-01 01:00:00 through 2026-09-25 10:00:00 UTC inclusive; no comparison period was requested (check 8).
Declared user snapshot: 2026-09-30 23:59:59 UTC. Build 3a0dbed21d2f45958aefa2887a0cadd8 succeeded 2026-11-09 11:16:56 UTC; build reconciliation checks are recorded as passing (checks 2–3).
Revenue group v1.1 defines valid success and charge timing. Counts are an ad hoc descriptive application, not a registered campaign attribution metric.
Inventory layers and build, inspect source schemas and event property keys, then quantify purchases and missing links.

Gold marketing is channel-month only. Silver provides validated purchase and profile detail; Bronze supplies source schemas and event properties. Stop: a campaign-level link and causal design are absent.
Sources partition users in this snapshot. Counts describe acquisition labels, not campaigns responsible for purchases (check 7).

rows: No campaign or UTM columns found; event JSON keys contain no campaign identifier (checks 6, 10).
First-touch source identifies the causing campaign
Channel is not a campaign and cannot establish causation (checks 4, 7).

items: 59 charges and 14 purchasers have unknown first-touch source. All 6,215 charge rows have user IDs; 4,546 lack checkout links and 4,490 lack session links. Off-session payments and uncaptured links have different meanings; neither count alone measures campaign coverage (checks 7–8).
Thirteen payment rows have reviewed source-amount corrections; review time is unknown (check 9).

The current repository registry SHA-256 differs from the registry SHA recorded at build. The builder SHA matches. Build-time reconciliation is historical; source fingerprints have not been independently recomputed, so current layer freshness is not verified.

There is no campaign identifier, user-level ad exposure or click-to-purchase mapping in the inspected schema and event properties. The absence of these fields prevents campaign assignment, irrespective of the share with a known channel.
Even a linked click would support an agreed attribution rule, not by itself prove incremental causal impact.
The supplied directory has no Git metadata; commit and download date are unavailable. Repository inspected 2026-11-09; hashes are recorded in run-notes.
Capture consent-appropriate campaign IDs and impression/click events with timestamps, stable identity linkage and purchase IDs; measure missing and ambiguous links.
Agree on the eligible purchases, attribution window, touchpoint precedence and treatment of renewals and unknowns before producing campaign attribution.
Use randomized holdouts or a defensible experiment to estimate incremental campaign effects, rather than treating assigned credit as causation.

Checks 01–11 are separate evidence logs; check 05 failed authorization on a table-valued PRAGMA and is retained. Check 10 used sqlite_master as a read-only alternative. All successful result sets were untruncated.
Inputs, SQL, results, build reconciliation and an index are saved beside this report.
